title: “-1” Industrializes Your Thinking. And That’s Why It Exposes Every Toxic Activity You Keep Defending.
summary: How “-1” turns work into a measurable operating system and exposes activities that cannot justify their value.

title: When AI Becomes More Honest Than You, “-1” Becomes Impossible to Ignore.
summary: AI can surface uncomfortable contradictions; “-1” converts those contradictions into measurable responsibility and consequences.

title: Technical Experts Who Never Become Strategic Thinkers Are Walking Into a Trap. “-1” Is the Final Evolution.
summary: Why technical competence alone is becoming insufficient, and why strategic thinking, measurement, AI literacy, and responsibility become the next layer.

title: Every Bad Hire Has a Penalty. Every Rejected Star Becomes Your Competitor’s Weapon.
summary: Recruiting already contains hidden penalties: the cost of a bad hire and the opportunity cost of rejecting high-value talent.

title: If Your Competitors Aren’t Angry by 11 A.M., Your Negative Price Guarantee Is Too Weak.
summary: One of the most useful direct-response provocations associated with Dan Kennedy is this: If nobody is uncomfortable with what you say, you are probably too safe to be remembered.

title: Your Company Is Not “Out of Money.” It’s Buried Under Dead Assets, Idle People, and Expensive Corporate Clutter.
summary: Garages full of objects nobody touches. Tools bought for one project and forgotten.

title: Buyer’s Remorse Is the Hidden Tax Weak Companies Make Customers Pay. “-1” Forces Them to Carry It Instead.
summary: Buyer’s remorse is one of the most expensive hidden taxes in every market. They invest money, time, attention, and emotional energy.

title: Copycats Can Copy Your Offer. They Can’t Survive Your Negative Price Guarantee
summary: In every market, there are copycats. They imitate the visible surface of the system.

title: Stop Hiring Salespeople to Feed a Leaking Business. Revenue Is Not Profit—and “-1” Exposes the Hole.
summary: The lazy growth plan is always the same: Because if your current business is leaking profit through unmeasured processes, unclear handoffs, rework, weak margins, slow cash collection, and operational chaos, adding more sales does not solve the problem.

title: Stop Calling It “Confidence.” It’s Anti-Expertise. “-1” Makes Ignorance Expensive Again.
summary: There is a difference between not knowing something and refusing to learn. There is a difference between making a mistake and protecting it with arrogance.
